audit_status.review_note: Reviewed for gatekeeping, fertility blessing, warrior language, lots, accessibility, treasury oversight, dedicated war spoil, religious-state administration, regional authority, and labor accountability.

verses.restored: Divisions of gatekeepers: from Korahites, Meshelemiah son of Kore from sons of Asaph/Ebiasaph.
Sons of Meshelemiah: Zechariah firstborn, Jediael second, Zebadiah third, Jathniel fourth,
Elam fifth, Jehohanan sixth, Eliehoenai seventh.
Sons of Obed-edom: Shemaiah firstborn, Jehozabad second, Joah third, Sacar fourth, Nethanel fifth,
Ammiel sixth, Issachar seventh, Peullethai eighth, for Divine blessed him.
To Shemaiah his son were born sons who ruled ancestral house, for they were mighty people of ability.
Sons of Shemaiah: Othni, Rephael, Obed, Elzabad, whose relatives Elihu and Semachiah were able people.
All these from sons of Obed-edom, they and sons and relatives, able with strength for service—sixty-two from Obed-edom.
Meshelemiah had sons and relatives, able people—eighteen.
Hosah from sons of Merari had sons: Shimri the chief, though not firstborn, father made him chief;
Hilkiah second, Tebaliah third, Zechariah fourth. All sons and relatives of Hosah were thirteen.
To these divisions of gatekeepers, chief people had duties corresponding to relatives to minister in house of YHWH.
They cast lots, small and great alike by ancestral house, for each gate.
Lot eastward fell to Shelemiah. For Zechariah his son, a counselor with insight, they cast lots, and his lot came northward.
For Obed-edom southward, and for sons the storehouse.
For Shuppim and Hosah westward, at Shallecheth gate by ascending highway, watch beside watch.
Eastward six Levites each day, northward four, southward four, and at storehouse two by two.
At colonnade westward, four at highway and two at colonnade.
These were divisions of gatekeepers from Korahites and sons of Merari.
Levites—their relatives—were over treasuries of house of Divine and treasuries of dedicated things.
Descendants of Ladan, Gershonites through Ladan, heads of ancestral houses: Jehieli.
Sons of Jehieli, Zetham and Joel his brother, were over treasuries of house of YHWH.
From Amramites, Izharites, Hebronites, and Uzzielites:
Shebuel son of Gershom son of Moses was ruler over treasuries.
His relatives through Eliezer: Rehabiah his son, Jeshaiah his son, Joram his son, Zichri his son, Shelomoth his son.
Shelomoth and relatives were over all treasuries of dedicated things that David the king, ancestral heads, commanders of thousands and hundreds, and army commanders had dedicated.
From wars and spoil they dedicated things to maintain house of YHWH.
All Samuel the seer, Saul son of Kish, Abner son of Ner, and Joab son of Zeruiah had dedicated—every dedicated thing was under hand of Shelomoth and relatives.
From Izharites, Chenaniah and sons were assigned to external business over Israel as officers and judges.
From Hebronites, Hashabiah and relatives, able people—one thousand seven hundred—had oversight west of Jordan for all work of YHWH and service of king.
From Hebronites, Jerijah was chief according to generations. In fortieth year of David's reign they were sought, and able people were found at Jazer of Gilead.
His relatives, able ancestral heads—two thousand seven hundred—David made overseers over Reubenites, Gadites, and half-Manasseh for every matter of Divine and matter of king.

translation_notes: Gatekeepers manage safety, access, property, and welcome; they should not become militarized bouncers or barriers to disabled and marginalized worshippers.
Obed-edom's many sons are called blessing, but fertility and number of children are not universal measures of Divine favor.
'Mighty' and 'able' should include reliability and skill, not only violent masculinity.
Lots distribute gates but do not guarantee fairness; accessibility, rotation, and oversight remain necessary.
Treasuries require transparent records, separation of duties, and protection against clerical or royal misuse.
War spoil dedicated to temple maintenance does not cleanse the violence or restore property to those from whom it was taken.
Samuel, Saul, Abner, Joab, and David all contribute to sacred treasury despite morally complex histories; donations do not purchase absolution.
External officers combine religious and royal matters, raising concerns about theocracy, policing, and institutional overreach.
Regional oversight across Jordan may reflect centralized control rather than local consent.
safety_note: Do not use gatekeeping to exclude, family size as blessing hierarchy, sacred treasury to launder war wealth, or religious officers as unaccountable police. Require accessibility, transparent finances, labor dignity, local voice, and separation of religious and coercive power.
